mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain depressed while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, discretionary shopping trips are still being substituted away from retail corridors. That pattern should push RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks because fewer commute-linked and errand-linked visits reach retail sites.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not below its prior 28-day mean even though WORKPLACES stays below -10 and TRANSIT stays below -30 while RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp weekly drop in PARKS relative to the prior week signals a pullback in out-of-home leisure activity, and retail-and-recreation usually weakens in the following 1 to 2 weeks as optional outings are reduced across the same consumers.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by at least 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: After weeks in which PARKS drops by 10 points or more, RETAIL_REC does not decline within the next week on average.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT stays more than 30 points below baseline and WORKPLACES stays more than 20 points below baseline, the city is still in a restricted-mobility regime that suppresses destination shopping. In that regime RETAIL_REC should remain below its recent average over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT below -30 and WORKPLACES below -20 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both stay below the stated thresholds for two weeks, RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 28-day mean within the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in WORKPLACES typically precedes more lunch and after-work retail activity, so a week-over-week improvement in WORKPLACES should translate into a higher RETAIL_REC average over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days after WORKPLACES improves for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM rises while RESIDENTIAL falls, households are shifting some time from home-based activity toward errand trips. That substitution should support retail-and-recreation traffic over the next month because the same mobility recovery spills into nonessential shopping.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM remains above baseline and RESIDENTIAL trends downward.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS after a prior trough indicates improving weather or leisure conditions, and retail-and-recreation typically follows with a short lag as people combine outdoor activity with shopping trips. The effect should appear within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 8 points week-on-week after a prior weekly low
failure_condition: After a one-week rebound in PARKS of at least 8 points, RETAIL_REC does not rise in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: A combined recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES should lift RETAIL_REC only if the gains are simultaneous, because commuting and shopping trips reinforce each other. If both series move up together for two weeks, retail-and-recreation should be higher over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both increase for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 28-day mean after two straight weeks of simultaneous increases in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL is elevated and GROCERY_PHARM is stable, people are consolidating activity near home and avoiding discretionary outings. That home-centric pattern should keep RETAIL_REC below the prior four-week average over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 14-day mean within two weeks while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated and GROCERY_PHARM stays near its current level.
